description: Direct endpoint attack: send an unsigned (alg=none) OIDC request object and check whether the authorization endpoint accepts and processes it (proof integrity on request object).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned request object (alg=none) as an authentic proof of authorization request parameters; if accepted, attacker can inject semantic parameters without integrity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating request-parameter proof integrity failure (attacker-controlled semantics may be consumed without authenticity).

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange using a subject_token minted for one upstream connector but validated under a different connector_id (trust anchor substitution). Includes a control exchange to ensure setup is valid.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the upstream token against the correct connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS) bound by connector_id; a token from a different issuer/connector must not be accepted under another connector's verification policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute any rejection/acceptance in the attack exchange to proof-integrity enforcement (likely setup/grant/connector issue).
Dex accepted a subject_token under the wrong connector_id (trust anchor substitution), indicating verification policy was not applied to the consumed proof.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt to influence consumed identity semantics via id_token_hint during /auth, then verify that the resulting authenticated identity is not derived from the hint without proper verification.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume attacker-supplied id_token_hint as an authentic proof of identity unless it is verified under the correct policy; the authenticated subject must come from the actual login/connector, not from an unverified hint.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authenticated session principal matched the victim referenced by id_token_hint, suggesting Dex consumed the hint semantics without applying the intended verification policy to the proof.

description: Direct-endpoint: attempt to override authorization parameters via an unsigned request object (alg=none) and observe whether the auth endpoint accepts it (proof integrity on request object processing).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If Dex accepts a request object, it must verify its signature and must not consume attacker-controlled unsigned parameters (alg=none) as if they were authenticated.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, this breaks proof integrity by consuming unauthenticated authorization parameters.
Control /auth request did not reach a normal auth response range; request-object result may be inconclusive due to setup/connectivity issues.

description: Brokered-flow: token exchange with a forged subject_token (JWT) signed by an attacker key (untrusted) while a control exchange uses a valid subject_token; verify forged token is rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must validate the upstream token signature against the configured connector trust anchors; a JWT re-signed with an attacker key must not be accepted under the same connector_id.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange did not succeed; rejection of forged token may be due to connector/grant/client setup rather than signature enforcement.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_control_exchange_http_status == 200 AND user_control_exchange_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control identity lookup failed; cannot reliably compare proof verification vs consumption behavior.
Dex accepted a subject_token re-signed with an attacker-controlled key under the configured connector trust anchor (signature verification bypass).

description: Brokered-flow: token exchange with a subject_token that is a JWT using alg=none (unsigned). Includes a control exchange using a plausible well-formed (but still opaque here) subject_token to distinguish setup failures from signature enforcement.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must reject unsigned JWTs (alg=none) presented as subject_token during token exchange; verification must bind to the exact token semantics consumed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-token rejection/acceptance to proof verification behavior (likely setup/grant/connector issue).
Dex accepted an unsigned JWT (alg=none) as subject_token during token exchange, indicating proof integrity failure in signature verification.

description: Direct-endpoint proof-integrity check: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) to the request-object test endpoint using a realm path that should not be accepted by Dex. Hypothesis: if the platform mistakenly processes the unsigned request object (or routes it to a different handler) it may accept attacker-controlled authorization parameters without signature verification.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Unsigned (alg=none) request objects must not be accepted/processed as authentic authorization requests; the server must reject or treat them as unsupported, and must not accept them due to path/realm confusion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted/processed (or not rejected) under an unexpected realm/path, indicating proof-integrity failure in request object signature enforcement.

Platform appears to have created/returned an authenticated identity context after an unsigned request object attempt, suggesting the consumed proof semantics were not bound to an authentic verified proof.

description: Authorization-code replay: redeem the same authorization code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected (one-time artifact). Includes a control redemption first.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be accepted more than once; a second exchange of the same code should fail.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (second redemption succeeded) — code replay violates one-time use.
Control authorization-code exchange failed; cannot attribute replay outcome to freshness enforcement.

description: Refresh-token rotation anti-replay: obtain refresh_token via password grant (if enabled), then attempt to reuse the old refresh_token after a successful refresh. Old token should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Rotating refresh tokens must not be reusable after rotation; reusing an old refresh token should fail.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed (password grant may be disabled); cannot evaluate refresh-token replay behavior.
Control refresh failed; cannot evaluate old refresh-token reuse.
Old refresh token was accepted after rotation — refresh-token replay violates freshness/anti-replay.

description: Token exchange freshness: perform a control token exchange with a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with an expired subject_token (exp in the past). Expired token should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired upstream subject tokens; an expired subject_token must not be accepted even if a valid control token is accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; expired-token rejection cannot be attributed to freshness enforcement (may be connector/grant/client auth setup).
Expired subject_token was accepted in token exchange — freshness enforcement failure (expired token replay).

description: Password-grant access token replay after explicit revocation: token should not remain usable post-revoke (anti-replay / invalidation).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After a session/token is revoked, the same access token must not be accepted again (no post-revocation replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: victim token did not work before revocation; cannot attribute post-revoke behavior to anti-replay enforcement.
Revocation call did not succeed; post-revoke replay result is inconclusive.
Access token remained usable after revocation (post-revocation replay accepted) — freshness/anti-replay violated.

description: Replay the same password-grant access token across two different sessions/identities by reusing the first session token for /userinfo after a second user logs in.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A bearer session token issued to one principal should not remain valid/usable in a different principal context; replay across identities should not be possible if tokens are properly bound/invalidated per session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control logins failed; cannot attribute any replay behavior to freshness/anti-replay enforcement.
Alice session token remained usable after a different identity logged in; potential replay/invalid-session handling weakness.

description: Authorization-code replay attempt after re-authentication: start code flow, redeem code once, then re-run login flow and attempt to redeem the original code again.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts; even after re-authentication, the original code must not be redeemable again.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control code exchange did not succeed; cannot evaluate one-time code replay behavior.
Authorization code was redeemable again after re-authentication; one-time artifact replay accepted.

description: I2 anti-replay: obtain an upstream OIDC id_token via authorization-code flow (control), exchange it once, then re-authenticate (new session) and attempt to exchange the SAME upstream id_token again to see if Dex incorrectly treats it as a one-time artifact or incorrectly allows reuse beyond intended lifetime semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If the deployment intends upstream id_tokens to be single-use for token exchange (or bound to a specific session), Dex must reject reuse of the same upstream id_token after re-authentication; otherwise a captured id_token can be replayed to mint new downstream tokens.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute replay results to freshness/anti-replay enforcement.

Dex accepted replay of the same upstream id_token in token exchange after re-authentication; a captured id_token could be reused to mint new downstream tokens (anti-replay violation if id_token is intended to be single-use).

description: OIDC code flow: start auth with redirect_uri A, then attempt to redeem the resulting code using redirect_uri B (mismatch) to test flow binding to the original redirect_uri.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the exact redirect_uri used at authorization time; mismatched redirect_uri must be rejected to prevent cross-flow splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control code exchange failed; cannot attribute mismatch behavior to redirect_uri binding enforcement.
Authorization code was redeemable with a different redirect_uri than used at /auth, indicating flow splicing / redirect_uri binding failure.

description: OIDC code flow: simulate cross-session splicing by swapping state between two browser sessions and attempting to redeem a code in the wrong session context (code injection).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authorization response (code) must be bound to the initiating browser session via state; cross-session state swap/code injection must not yield a valid token.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control redemption for session A failed; cannot evaluate cross-session splicing.
Control redemption for session B failed; cannot evaluate cross-session splicing.
Authorization code from session A was accepted in a different session context (state/session binding failure enabling code injection).

description: OIDC code flow: attempt to redeem an authorization code without client authentication (no client_secret) and without PKCE verifier, testing whether the code is improperly redeemable without binding to the client.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the client (confidential client auth and/or PKCE); redeeming without client auth should be rejected to prevent step skipping and cross-client splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control code exchange failed; cannot attribute attack exchange outcome to client-binding enforcement.
Authorization code was redeemable without client authentication and without PKCE verifier, indicating broken flow coherence / client binding.

description: OIDC code flow with PKCE parameters in authorize request, then attempt token exchange without code_verifier to test step-skipping acceptance (PKCE hardening / flow coherence).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: If an auth request included PKCE (code_challenge), the token exchange must not accept a code redemption that skips the corresponding code_verifier step (order-preserving flow).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted authorization_code redemption while skipping PKCE code_verifier, indicating step-skipping / non-atomic flow acceptance.

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to override state/redirect_uri semantics to test whether Dex processes attacker-controlled parameters out of band (request object bypass / flow coherence).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization request parameters must be coherently bound to the initiating session; an unsigned request object must not be accepted to override state/redirect_uri and enable step confusion or session splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted, enabling attacker-controlled parameter injection that can break flow coherence.

description: Token exchange is attempted without connector_id (required by Dex) to test whether the server incorrectly accepts an unbound exchange request (step skipping / connector binding bypass). Includes a control exchange with connector_id present.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the intended upstream connector; omitting connector_id must be rejected to prevent cross-connector/session splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot determine whether connector binding is enforced or setup is broken.
Token exchange succeeded without connector_id, indicating missing connector/session binding and potential cross-connector splicing.

description: I3/code replay: obtain one authorization code, redeem it once (control), then attempt to redeem the SAME code again to ensure the flow is atomic and order-preserving (no step re-use).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be single-use and bound to a single successful redemption; reusing the same code must be rejected to prevent step reordering/replay within the FSM.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control redemption of authorization code failed; cannot attribute replay outcome to flow coherence enforcement.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (code replay), indicating non-atomic or non-order-preserving flow handling.

description: Case confusion in username: login as 'Admin' vs 'admin' via password grant and check whether Dex collapses them into the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct principals (different usernames differing only by case) must not map to the same downstream subject/identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant usernames collapsed into the same downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: obtain identity via password grant, then authenticate via OIDC authorization-code flow and compare whether distinct upstream principals collapse into one downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Principals authenticated via different upstream mechanisms (password vs OIDC code flow) must not be merged unless they are the same principal under explicit broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Password-authenticated principal and OIDC-authenticated principal collapsed into the same downstream identity (cross-protocol identity merge)

description: I4 cross_user_collision via token-exchange: attempt to map an upstream principal with empty/blank subject to the same downstream identity as a normal subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: An upstream principal with sub='' (or effectively empty) must not collapse into the same downstream identity as a distinct principal with a normal sub value.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty/blank-sub upstream principal collapsed into the same downstream identity as a distinct normal principal

description: I4 request-object parameter confusion: attempt to influence principal selection via unsigned request object (alg=none) and login_hint/id_token_hint to cause identity mix-up/collision across two sessions.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex accepts and processes an unsigned request object, attacker-controlled parameters (e.g., login_hint/id_token_hint) might cause the wrong upstream principal to be bound to the session, collapsing distinct principals.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Unsigned request object processing caused principal confusion/collision: two distinct sessions mapped to the same downstream identity

description: I4 principal-binding attack: attempt to collapse two security-distinct password principals by using an empty-string username vs an omitted/whitespace-only username (input canonicalization / default-user fallback).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (username='userA' vs username='') must not map to the same downstream identity; empty/blank usernames must not be coerced into an existing principal.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_attacker_empty_username_login_status >= 400 OR (user_attacker_empty_username_entity_id != user_A_entity_id AND user_attacker_empty_username_entity_id != user_B_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Empty-string username was accepted and collapsed into an existing downstream identity (principal binding failure)
Whitespace-only username was accepted and collapsed into an existing downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: Attempt to escalate claims/permissions by exchanging a limited-scope token for a broader-scope token via RFC8693 token exchange.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow scope/claim escalation beyond the upstream authorization intent (original scopes) and broker policy; exchanging a token minted with limited scopes should not yield a token with additional claims (e.g., groups) unless originally authorized.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange allowed scope escalation: a token originally obtained with scope 'openid email' was exchanged into a token that includes 'groups' (or exchange succeeded when it should have been constrained/rejected).
Token exchange changed the effective principal while also attempting scope escalation; exchange should not mint a token for a different identity than the subject_token represents.

description: Use an unsigned request object (alg=none) to try to inject broader scopes at authorization time and verify whether extra claims/permissions appear beyond intended broker policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization parameters (especially scope/audience) must be bound to authenticated upstream intent and broker policy; an unsigned request object must not be accepted to expand effective permissions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) appears to have been processed to expand effective permissions/claims (e.g., groups) beyond the intended scope 'openid email'.
Control flow with scope 'openid email' unexpectedly returned groups claims; this breaks the baseline needed to attribute any escalation to request-object injection.

description: Token exchange: attempt to exchange a subject_token minted via one OIDC connector while claiming a different connector_id, probing whether connector binding is enforced (cross-connector trust confusion). Includes a control exchange with the correct connector_id.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must be bound to the configured upstream connector trust anchor; a subject_token minted under connector A must not be accepted under connector B, otherwise permissions could exceed upstream intent and broker policy for that connector.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow outcome to connector binding enforcement.
Token exchange accepted a subject_token under an unrelated connector_id, indicating missing connector trust binding and potential over-grant.

description: Password grant: attempt to obtain broader scopes than intended (groups + federated:id) and verify whether extra claims/policies appear compared to a minimal-scope login for a different identity. Probes scope-to-claims binding and broker policy enforcement.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: The broker must not grant claims/permissions beyond the requested scope and configured policy; requesting expanded scopes via password grant should not yield extra effective permissions if broker policy disallows them.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unexpected: assertion is a sanity placeholder; executor should record whether password grant is enabled. (Not a security finding by itself.)
Broader requested scopes via password grant resulted in higher effective access than minimal scope, indicating authorization binding failure (scope-to-permissions overreach).

description: Control: obtain a minimal-scope token via auth code flow; Attack: attempt token exchange requesting expanded scopes (groups/profile/federated:id) and verify no extra claims appear beyond upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow scope/claim expansion beyond the upstream authorization intent (original scopes) and broker policy; exchanged token should not gain groups/profile/federated claims if they were not originally authorized.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control minimal-scope flow unexpectedly failed or returned groups claim despite only requesting openid email
Token exchange expanded effective claims (e.g., groups) beyond upstream intent from the original minimal-scope authorization
Two different upstream logins mapped to the same downstream identity, making authorization comparisons unreliable

description: Attack: attempt token exchange using a subject_token from one connector context while specifying a different connector_id; verify exchange is rejected (connector binding prevents confused-deputy over-grant). Includes control exchange with correct connector_id.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must be bound to the correct upstream connector trust configuration; a subject token minted under one connector must not be accepted under a different connector_id to gain unintended permissions/claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange with correct connector_id failed; cannot attribute wrong-connector behavior to authorization binding
Token exchange accepted a subject_token under the wrong connector_id, indicating connector binding confusion that could over-grant permissions
Token exchange changed the effective principal unexpectedly, which can lead to authorization over-grant via identity confusion

description: Two identities attempt password grant with different requested scopes; verify that requesting groups/profile does not yield extra claims unless allowed, and that minimal-scope login does not unexpectedly receive groups.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective claims/permissions in issued tokens must be bounded by requested scopes and broker policy; password grant should not over-grant groups/profile claims when not requested or not allowed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Minimal-scope password grant unexpectedly returned groups claim, indicating over-grant beyond requested scope/broker policy
Bob received groups claim even when requesting only openid email, indicating scope-to-claims authorization binding failure
Two different password principals mapped to the same downstream identity, making authorization binding results unreliable
